passages.heading: Overview of leave
passages.passage_text: Maple Ridge Services offers paid holidays, paid time off, sick leave, bereavement leave, parental leave, and time off for jury duty and voting. This guide explains how much leave you receive and how to request it.

passages.heading: Paid holidays
passages.passage_text: The company observes nine paid holidays each year: New Year's Day, Martin Luther King Jr. Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, the day after Thanksgiving, and Christmas Day.

passages.heading: Paid time off
passages.passage_text: Full-time employees receive 20 days of paid leave per year. Paid time off builds up a little each pay period. After three years of employment, this increases to 25 days per year. Part-time employees receive paid time off based on their scheduled hours.

passages.heading: Requesting paid time off
passages.passage_text: Request paid time off in Maple Connect. For three or more days in a row, submit your request at least two weeks in advance. Your manager approves all requests. You can carry over any unused days into the next year.

passages.heading: Sick leave
passages.passage_text: Employees receive six paid sick days per year, separate from paid time off. If you are sick, tell your manager before your shift starts. A doctor's note is required after three sick days in a row.

passages.heading: Bereavement leave
passages.passage_text: If an immediate family member dies, you can take up to three paid days off. Immediate family includes a spouse or partner, child, parent, sibling, or grandparent. You can take one paid day off for the death of another relative.

passages.heading: Parental leave
passages.passage_text: After 12 months of employment, employees can take six weeks of paid parental leave following the birth or adoption of a child. Tell your manager and HR at least 30 days before your leave starts when possible.

passages.heading: Jury duty and voting
passages.passage_text: The company pays your regular pay for up to 10 days of jury duty. If your work schedule does not allow time to vote on Election Day, you can take up to two hours of paid time off to vote.

passages.heading: Leave for new employees
passages.passage_text: Sick leave is available from your first day. Paid time off can be used once you complete your 90-day introductory period, although it starts building up from your first day. For more about the introductory period, see HR-01, New-Hire Orientation.
